newsitem.title: UK: Press Digest - British Sundays - Feb 23.
newsitem.headline: Press Digest - British Sundays - Feb 23.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- RACAL TO BE BROKEN UP IN 'EXIT PLAN'

Sir Ernest Harrison, 70 year old chairman of Racal Electronics is said to be engaged in secret discussions about a spectacular exit from the company he built up from tiny beginnings over three decades. He is planning to break up the electronics group in a series of disposals, mergers and management buy outs.
-- US POWER GROUP PLANS OFFER FOR YORKSHIRE ELECTRICITY

An American utility is lining up a 1.4bn bid for Yorkshire Electricity, one of the last two independent power distributors on the stockmarket. American Electric Power one of the US's largest electricity companies based in Columbus Ohio is thought to be poised to make a bid worth about 860p a share in cash for Yorkshire. An offer could come as early as this week.
-- BRANSON HAS FLOTATION PLANS FOR VIRGIN RAIL

Richard Branson intends to float Virgin Rail on the London stockmarket in a move that would herald his return to the quoted sector for the first time since he took Virgin Group back into private ownership in 1988.
-- EQUITY & LAW FOR SALE WITH 1BN PRICE TAG

French insurance giant AXA-UAP has put Equity & Law its British life assurance arm up for sale for up to 1bn while it decides how to rationalise its British interests including a majority stake in Sun Life and Provincial.
-- MONDEX GRABS GIROVEND STAKE

Mondex UK, the electronic cash card joint venture between NatWest and Midland Bank is taking a 10 per cent stake in Girovend, the cashless systems business, which is due to float next month. The listing will value Girovend at about 25m and Mondex is thought to have paid around 2m for its stake.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- GEC AND BAE ARE TIPPED FOR 16BN MERGER

The General Electric Company(GEC) and British Aerospace(BAe) are expected to enter talks this year about an alliance that could create a British defence equipment colossus valued at 16bn. Whitehall, City and industry insiders believe the chances are increasing of a full merger that could produce the western world's fourth largest defence supplier.
-- LABOUR PLANS A SHAKE-UP OF THE UTILITY REGULATORS

A Labour government would move rapidly to re-organise the system of utility regulation by establishing boards of non- executive directors to sit alongside industry watchdogs. Labour's trade and industry team headed by Margaret Beckett is believed to see reform of the regulatory structure as one of its top priorities alongside a sweeping overhaul of government competition policy.
-- PEARSON SCAM WOMAN REVEALED

The Penguin USA executive who cost Pearson 100m in losses and legal fees has been identified as Christina Galatro, a former credit manager in the New Jersey office of the publisher. Galatro who is in her mid fifties was dismissed two weeks ago after Penguin executives discovered that for the past six years she had been giving unauthorized discounts to booksellers and hiding them as assets in the company's accounts.
-- LEGAL QUAGMIRE THREATENS BROWN'S WINDFALL TAX

Labour's plans for a windfall tax to extract between 3bn and 10bn from privatized utilities could run into a procedural quagmire according to an authority on drafting legislation. Despite the announcement by Gordon Brown, shadow chancellor, that Labour had legal advice that its tax would be achievable, Joe Durkin of Rees & Freres stated that a windfall tax bill along the lines proposed by Labour would be a "hybrid" bill.
-- TUCKEY FACES DTI BAN FROM THE BOARDROOM

The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) is seeking to ban Andrew Tuckey, Barings deputy chairman when the bank went bust two years ago from acting as a director. The DTI issued a summons on Friday against Tuckey under the Company Directors Disqualification Act in an action that, if successful could result in a ban of up to 15 years. Friends say he is going to contest the action.
THE OBSERVER
-- LABOUR TO BLOCK NEW GAS PLANTS

A Labour government is set to curb the rush by electricity generators to build new gas fired power stations. If elected the party will clampdown on applications for new gas plants in an attempt to secure a continuing market for coal.
-- LONRHO REOPENS BIDDING RACE FOR PRINCESS HOTELS

Saudi investor Prince al Waleed faces new rivals in the 350m race to buy Lonrho's Princess chain of luxury hotels. The conglomerate has cancelled a deal that gave the prince exclusive negotiating rights.
-- BA WOULD GIVE UP HEATHROW SLOTS TO CLINCH MERGER

British Airways is considering giving away take off and landing slots at Heathrow Airport if that is the price of clinching approval from Brussels for its alliance with American Airlines. The airline had insisted that it would give up slots only if it could sell them to other carriers which could bring it more than 300m. But now it privately admits that it may have to cede control over the assets for no return in order to placate European competition authorities.
-- EMU BANKER WARNS ON DEFICIT RULES

Tough rules designed to keep countries on the fiscal straight and narrow once the join the single European currency mean some will have to run an underlying budget surplus according to Wim Duisenberg, head of the Dutch central bank and the man tipped to take over the job at the proposed European Central Bank (ECB).
-- PRODUCER'S THREAT TO QUIT PEARSON

Media Company Pearson is facing the threat of a revolt among its leading television producers and writers if it fails to retain the services of Greg Dyke, the chief executive of the group's TV subsidiary, Channel 5.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- HARRODS SCRAPS FLOTATION
Harrods has abandoned plans for a stock market flotation which its Egyptian owners, the Fayed brothers had hoped might value the prestigious Knightsbridge store at up to 2bn.
-- NATWEST JOINS SCOTAM RACE

National Westminster Bank has emerged as a last minute bidder for Scottish Amicable, the mutual life insurer. It has signed a confidentiality agreement to gain access to the information it needs to frame a bid which must be submitted by Friday.
-- HIGH TECH FIRM GOES WEST

Superscape the most successful of the trio of quoted British virtual reality companies is expected to switch its allegiance to Nasdaq, the US high tech stock exchange, following the shift of its headquarters from Hampshire to California. With Virtuality now in the hands of administrators a once promising London mini-sector could be reduced to just one company - Division.
-- AVIS FLOTATION PLANS

The PR machine for the flotation of Avis Europe is cranking into gear with Friday scheduled for the publication of a pathfinder prospectus and pricing range for the car rental firm. Avis is expected to be valued at up to 700m.
-- APPROVAL FOR BT MERGER PLANS WITH MCI

There is growing evidence that BT could gain regulatory approval as early as May for its proposed merger with MCI. BT and MCI had said a timetable for the merger should see regulatory approval reached by the autumn.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- KOHL IS WARNED AGAINST EMU BY GERMAN ECONOMISTS

Europe's controversial moves towards monetary union receive another blow today as a leading German economist, former Bundesbank board member Dr Wilhelm Noelling, threatens to take his government to court if it tries to bend the rules.
-- BILLION POUND FLU BOOSTER FOR GLAXO

Drugs giant Glaxo is one step from launching a world beating anti-flu drug that could generate sales of more than 1bn a year. The company will begin the third and final stage of clinical trials for the drug Zanamivir, being developed with Australian company Biota.
-- LABOUR THREATENS PROFITS TO INVESTORS IN TRAIN LEASING COMPANY

Labour is threatening to block huge profits for investors in the last privatized train leasing company waiting for a takeover bid. If Labour wins the election Angel Train Contracts will not enjoy the massive windfalls of Porterbrook and Evesholt.
-- SOCIETIES TAKE SHOT AT MIGS

Leading building societies are looking at ways to end the scandal of MIGs - mortgage indemnity guarantees. Thousands were left stranded during the property slum when they learned they were not personally covered by MIGs even though they paid premiums as high as 1,000 to cover a typical 50,000 mortgage.
-- NORTHERN ROCK'S 1M TO SOFTEN FLOAT BLOW TO DISABLED

Northern Rock is giving 1m to charity to help the disabled left out in the cold by its 1.25 bn flotation. The move will blunt criticism over the way Northern Rock and other converting building societies treat disabled savers
